issue_context.title: `DataFrame.diff` on `datetime64` returns result inconsistent with `Series.diff`
issue_context.body:
#### Code Sample, a copy-pastable example if possible

```python
>>> pd.Series(['NaT', '2019-01-01', '2019-01-02'], dtype='datetime64[ns]').diff()
0      NaT
1      NaT
2   1 days
dtype: timedelta64[ns]

>>> pd.Series(['NaT', '2019-01-01', '2019-01-02'], dtype='datetime64[ns]').to_frame().diff()
                             0
0                          NaT
1 -88855 days +00:12:43.145224
2              1 days 00:00:00
```

#### Problem description

Doing `.diff()` on a `DataFrame` of `datetime64` should yield exactly time deltas in exactly the same way as on the `Series` i.e. index `(1,0)` in the `DataFrame` above should be `NaT`, not an overflown timedelta64.

Hi @batterseapower, I copy-pasted the same code and was able to reproduce the bug.
I did some deep dive and found out that for dataframe(ndim=2), a function diff_2d in algos.pyx is being used which is written in cython.
For series type, there is another logic which has a comment 
`       # need to make sure that we account for na for datelike/timedelta
        # we don't actually want to subtract these i8 numbers`
which i believe is handling the NaT values properly by some mask and i was not able to find this mask code in diff_2d function.

Just to be sure i put a systemtrace and got the following output.
